pill.desc: pale yellow, oval, biconvex, film-coated tablet

tell: An SGLT2 inhibitor whose first listed indication is reducing cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalization.

clues.text: Plasma protein binding is 86.2%, and a high-fat meal lowers exposure by only about 16%, so food is not clinically relevant. Most of the dose is excreted in urine (54.4%) and feces (41.2%).
A free base rather than a salt, with a molecular weight of 450.91. A non-hygroscopic powder that is very slightly soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 10 mg and 25 mg tablets, taken once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated in hypersensitivity to the drug or its excipients, and angioedema has occurred.

Heart failure, to cut cardiovascular death and hospitalization; chronic kidney disease at risk of progression; cardiovascular death in type 2 diabetes with established heart disease; glycemic control from age 10.
Inhibits SGLT2, the main kidney transporter reabsorbing glucose, so urinary glucose excretion rises; it also reduces sodium reabsorption.
The generic name begins with E and has thirteen letters.
